newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: IBCA assigns ratings to SAfrican local authorities.
newsitem.headline: IBCA assigns ratings to SAfrican local authorities.

text.p: Rating Agency IBCA said on Wednesday it had assigned credit ratings to four South African municipalities and would publish ratings for others in the coming months.

The Khayalami Metropolitan Council was accorded an AA- long-term rating and an A1 short-term rating. The Midrand and Kempton Park/Tembisa metropolitan local councils were accorded a BBB long-term rating and an A3 short-term rating.
The Lethabong Metropolitan Local Council was rated A- in the long term and A2 in the short term.
The IBCA said the development of a rating system would clarify the risk profiles of local governments and would assist them in procuring funding and loans.
"We believe that this information will be critical not only for capital market participants, but also for service providers and contractors," the IBCA said in a statement.
Cash-flow problems faced by local governments had the capacity to be turned around and over time many of the problems faced, like services and payments, would be resolved, the agency said.
With the government making efforts to reduce its budget deficit, the local authorities will have to provide most of the essential services and to do so they would have to borrow substantially.

The IBCA said while it had reservations whether there were sufficient skills to conduct borrowings in a prudent manner, many of the entities it had rated did have sufficient expertise, provided they balanced political pressures and financial resources.
